concept_thesis: A full-size chair half-released from a raw white foam block is milled to fit a human body it can never hold: it invites a sitter, but the soft foam would crush under one. Human identity survives only as the chair's ergonomics; authorship survives only as the toolpath. The image holds the pause mid-process, between offer and refusal.
notes_for_material_specialist: The white foam is NOT a metal and must not be parameterised as one; its look (matte, dry, granular, beaded, no gloss, not marble, not snow) is carried entirely by subject.description, which leads the prompt. Only real metal belongs in materials. Make materials[0] the robot tool head: the spindle housing and ball-end mill, brushed steel with low reflectivity and a dust-coated, powder-dulled finish (imperfections such as white powder film and clinging foam beads), role 'machine presence, secondary, out of focus at right edge'. This is the element most at risk of disappearing, and without it the chair reads as hand-carved. materials[1] should be the slim black steel frame of the glass panel: matte blackened or oxidized steel, low reflectivity, flat curvature, faint dust film. Do not use liquid or polished chrome anywhere; nothing mirror-like should compete with the foam, and no metal terms should transfer onto the chair. Lighting suggestions (your call): a single raking side key from the left, medium-soft, neutral to slightly warm gallery tone, low or no fill, high contrast in a dark gallery so the foam is the only light-bearing substance; it should graze the terraced steps to reveal them without creating specular glints on the foam. The environment is a dark empty gallery, with no windows or bright reflections that could resolve into figures.

subject.description: half-carved plain chair emerging from raw matte white foam block on dark reflective gallery floor. The seat and front legs are finished with fine toolpath ridges; the backrest is still fused into the uncut rectangular block, which shows coarse terraced roughing steps. Dry, granular, beaded foam surfaces with no gloss. A thin scatter of white chips and beads on the floor around the base. At the right frame edge, cropped and out of focus, a black-framed glass panel with a faint powder film and a dust-coated white robot tool head behind it. The chair is empty.
subject.human_treatment: only through the chair's human scale and seat shape; no person, body part, silhouette or reflection anywhere

visual_hypothesis: If one plain, archetypal four-legged chair visibly emerges from a matte white foam block (finished seat and front legs, backrest still fused into a rough rectangular block cut in coarse terraced steps), standing directly on a dark polished gallery floor with no plinth, shot from a low asymmetric three-quarter angle with the chair on the left third, then a small model will read 'carved from a block' from the block-to-chair transition, and will read foam rather than marble from the terraced steps and dry granular faces. A thin scatter of white chips around the base implies the process; one cropped, out-of-focus black-framed glass panel with a dust-coated robot tool head behind it at the right edge keeps the machine present but secondary. The dark floor gives the chair one long, clean reflection with nothing else in it.
